chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, by his chain, raising it, said:
Whoever claims that the Imam needs what is in the hands of the people, then he is a disbeliever. Rather, it is the people who are in need that the Imam accept from them.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Take charity from their wealth, by which you cleanse them and purify them.”

key_terms.النَّاسِ: the people; the community of believers
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely appointed authority and guide
key_terms.تُزَكِّيهِمْ: it purifies and increases them in spiritual refinement
key_terms.كَافِرٌ: a disbeliever; one holding a belief counted as kufr in this context
key_terms.يَقْبَلَ: to accept; to receive from them

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam need the wealth of the people, or do the people benefit by giving to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the Imam is not dependent on people's possessions, and that attributing such need to the Imam is a false and grave belief. Rather, the spiritual benefit belongs to the people when the Imam accepts from them, as indicated by the Qur'anic principle that charity purifies its giver.
